scope: Single new U01-to-U02 transition and its displayed context only; root separately reviews whole-film checkpoints. This file does not approve the whole film.
method: Actually viewed existing34-frame full boundary board and34 head-window board (all18 dissolve frames plus8 frames each side) and native output f110 PNG. No continuous playback, source scan or media edit.

observations.viewpoint_and_movement: U01 is a centered frontal approach/reverse-track view; U02 becomes a clear right-facing profile moving across a crosswalk. The directional/camera change is intentionally large and visible. Chronological boundary samples show the linear superimposition evolving across18frames, not an extra one-frame switch; whether it feels abrupt at speed is unverified.
observations.head_scale: Broad head-to-shoe size and head height are reasonably close. Face orientation differs by approximately a frontal-to-side view, so eye/nose/mouth contours cannot line up despite similar scale.
observations.face_double_exposure: The middle overlap, approximately4.5–4.8seconds, visibly combines a front face and a right-facing profile, producing two facial outlines/eyes and layered hair. Native f110 at4.583seconds clearly shows this. It is a conspicuous crossfade, not a seamless turn or exact matched-face outfit switch.
observations.body_and_gait: Front torso and profile torso, held bag-strap hand and lower swinging arm occupy different positions. Different foot phases and black skirt/navy-trouser contours overlap. Pure-source context frames before and after show a coherent full person with complete shoes; no additional main-body collapse outside the fade is visible in this context.
observations.outfit_readability: Ivory blazer/white tee/dark trousers/brown bag are legible before the overlap; white short-sleeve shirt/black A-line skirt/blue bag are legible after. Transition frames temporarily obscure exact silhouette through garment overlap. Edit receipt reports4.25seconds of clear non-overlapped outfit per source; this arithmetic is not an audience-readability pass.
observations.crowd: Front-depth commuters in U01 blend into lateral-crosswalk commuters in U02. Several background heads/limbs are doubled during the fade; the figures do not conspicuously occlude the principal outfit in the displayed pure-source context. Fine distant-person anatomy is not certified.
observations.rigid_background: Building/window grids, trees, paving and crosswalk stripes occupy distinct perspectives and visibly double. Pure-source boundary context restores one rigid scene; no unexpected black frame, geometric melting or lingering double exposure beyond the intended fade is observed.
observations.subjective_style: Advertising attraction, decisive urban pace, normal-speed eye comfort and success against the user feedback are deliberately unassessed by this still-boundary review.

conclusion: This source pair can be shown as a direction test with the frontal-to-profile face/body/crowd double exposure disclosed. No additional checkpoint defect requires a trial-and-error re-edit before the user sees it. The visible angle transition is substantial, and comfort/pace/advertising impact require normal-speed user playback.
limitations: This reviewer inspected the join context, not a complete normal-speed playback.
A technical decode and18-frame transition do not establish pleasant perception.
Full-film source QA and whole-film checkpoints remain separate records.
The fade is not used here to declare identity, anatomy, crowds or background universally error-free.
